pages.text: For a traditional curing setup or decorative storage, tobacco can be hung in $(thing)16-leaf bunches$() instead of loaded into a Drying Rack. In Survival, hold at least $(item)16 identical raw or cured leaves$(), sneak, and right-click the $(thing)underside$() of a sturdy block. Exactly 16 leaves are stored. In Creative mode, one held leaf is sufficient to place the 16-leaf bunch. Already-cured leaves hang immediately and keep their cure, quality, and other processing data.

pages.title: Same Tobacco Cure
pages.text: A hanging bunch uses the same base curing times, quality calculation, interruptions, rain damage, cure-color stages, and priority as the rack: $(thing)Fire → Flue → Sun → Air$(). Raw and finished bunches also keep visible variety-specific leaf coloration. Break either half to recover all 16 stored leaves with their processing data.

pages.title: Pergola Sun Curing
pages.text: Because the bunch hangs under a support block, vertical sky above it is impossible. Sun Curing instead requires a horizontal neighboring $(item)air$() block beside either half that can see the sky and has sky light 14+ during daytime. This makes long $(item)beam / gap / beam / gap$() pergolas and slatted curing sheds valid.

pages.title: Covered Air Curing
pages.text: With no qualifying side-sky opening, a dry covered bunch Air Cures. A lit Campfire directly below the bottom of the bunch enables Fire Curing. Clean Flue Curing requires a nearby lit Flue Firebox, no side rain, no direct campfire below, and no nearby fire/campfire smoke source. Once Fire has been used it remains the final priority over later exposure; Flue likewise remains above Sun/Air.

pages.title: Traditional, Not Automated
pages.text: Hanging bunches are manual storage/curing blocks. They expose no hopper, funnel, Mechanical Arm, item capability, or Display Link source. Create fan airflow may still accelerate a valid curing environment. Use Drying Racks when item logistics and automated extraction matter.
